title: "Load More" functionality doesn't work when passing in searchState to component using InfiniteHits
body:
**Setup:**

* An "All Results" component that displays limited # of results for various categories
* A "Show More" component using `InfiniteHits` widget that displays certain # of results but ideally would add more results after clicking "Load More"

**Desired Behavior**

* "All Results" component shows first as you type in a query and each category section of results has a "Show more" link to bring in the "Show More" component.
* We want to preserve the current query and show the same results as displayed on "All Results" component and as you click "Load More", more results would get added on.

If I don't pass in the current `searchState` prop to the "Show more" results component, the Load More works just fine, but the current query isn't present.

When I do pass it in, the current query is preserved and the same results show, but the Load More stops working (is not disabled).

In the end, passing `searchState` that has a non-empty `query` to the `InstantSearch` wrapping `InfiniteHits`, seems to break the Load More functionality and it's not very obvious why, at least to me. Unsure if I'm missing something or if there's a better way of doing this, but let me know if anyone has any ideas.

**Update:**

After some debugging, I located part of thethe issue which was within `connectInfiniteHits` in the `refine` function. Basically the `searchState` I pass in with the current query `{query: "some text"}`  overwrites the `searchState` that is generated somewhere else and passed into `refine`. This loses the `page` key-value from the internally generated `searchState` and thus continues to reset to page 1 since `page` isn't found in `searchState`.

Need to do some more digging as to where the `searchState` for `refine` is getting passed in from, but wherever it is, it should just merge in the `searchState` prop that we pass into `InstantSearch` instead of having it completely replaced.
